content_voiceover: This slide reinforces PCH, and note the reminder at the top that this is not PNH, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, a common mix-up on boards because the names sound alike. PCH is also called Donath-Landsteiner hemolytic anemia. It's an autoimmune hemolytic anemia caused by a biphasic antibody, one that binds red cells and fixes complement in the cold, then triggers intravascular hemolysis when warmed. It's seen predominantly in pediatric patients, typically following a viral infection. The diagnostic test, the Donath-Landsteiner test, mixes patient serum with red cells at cold temperature first, then incubates at thirty-seven degrees and looks for hemolysis. In the image, tube A is the control, kept at thirty-seven degrees throughout, and shows no hemolysis, clear supernatant. Tube B was chilled first, then warmed, and shows visible hemolysis, a dark, lysed sample. That color difference between A and B is the positive Donath-Landsteiner result.
keypoints: PCH equals Donath-Landsteiner hemolytic anemia, NOT PNH -- common board mix-up
Biphasic antibody: binds RBCs and fixes complement in cold, lyses at 37 degrees C
Classically seen in children after a viral infection
Positive Donath-Landsteiner test: hemolysis only after cold-then-warm incubation
